nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field, $d \in K$ and $p_i, p_j, p_k \in K^2$. When $d = 0$, this step costs one unit and returns the value of ON-SEGMENT$(p_i, p_j, p_k)$; when $d \neq 0$, it costs nothing and returns false.
nodes.title: Collinear-endpoint step of SEGMENTS-INTERSECT

nodes.summary: For $p = (x_p, y_p)$ and $q = (x_q, y_q)$ in $K^2$, where $K$ is a linearly ordered field, the cross product is $p \times q = x_p y_q - x_q y_p$ (CLRS equation (33.1)).
nodes.title: Cross product of plane vectors

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field and $p, q, r \in K^2$. If $r$ lies on the closed segment from $p$ to $q$, then the direction $(r - p) \times (q - p)$ is zero, that is, $r$ is collinear with $p$ and $q$.
nodes.title: Points of a segment have direction zero

nodes.summary: For points $p_i, p_j, p_k \in K^2$, where $K$ is a linearly ordered field, CLRS's DIRECTION$(p_i, p_j, p_k)$ is the cross product $(p_k - p_i) \times (p_j - p_i)$.
nodes.title: Direction of three points

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field and $p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4 \in K^2$. Suppose the directions $(p_1 - p_3) \times (p_4 - p_3)$ and $(p_2 - p_3) \times (p_4 - p_3)$ are both zero and the closed segments $p_1 p_2$ and $p_3 p_4$ have a common point. Then $p_1$ or $p_2$ lies on the segment $p_3 p_4$, or $p_3$ or $p_4$ lies on the segment $p_1 p_2$.
nodes.title: Collinear case of segment intersection

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field and $p, q, r \in K^2$ with $p \neq q$. If $(r - p) \times (q - p) = 0$, then $r = p + \mu (q - p)$ for some $\mu \in K$.
nodes.title: Points with direction zero lie on the line

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field and $p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4 \in K^2$. Suppose the directions $(p_1 - p_3) \times (p_4 - p_3)$ and $(p_2 - p_3) \times (p_4 - p_3)$ are nonzero with opposite signs, and so are $(p_3 - p_1) \times (p_2 - p_1)$ and $(p_4 - p_1) \times (p_2 - p_1)$. Then the closed segments $p_1 p_2$ and $p_3 p_4$ have a common point.
nodes.title: Properly crossing segments meet

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field, write $(u_1, u_2) \times (v_1, v_2) = u_1 v_2 - v_1 u_2$ for the cross product on $K^2$, and let $p, q, r \in K^2$. If $r$ is collinear with $p$ and $q$, that is, the direction $(r - p) \times (q - p)$ is zero, and ON-SEGMENT$(p, q, r)$ is true, that is, $r$ lies in the bounding box of $p$ and $q$, then $r$ lies on the closed segment from $p$ to $q$.
nodes.title: A collinear point in the bounding box lies on the segment

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field and $p, q, r \in K^2$. If $r$ lies on the closed segment from $p$ to $q$, then ON-SEGMENT$(p, q, r)$ is true, that is, $r$ lies in the bounding box of $p$ and $q$.
nodes.title: Points of a segment lie in its bounding box

nodes.summary: For points $p_i = (x_i, y_i)$, $p_j = (x_j, y_j)$ and $p_k = (x_k, y_k)$ in $K^2$, where $K$ is a linearly ordered field, CLRS's ON-SEGMENT$(p_i, p_j, p_k)$ is the Boolean that is true exactly when $p_k$ lies in the bounding box of $p_i$ and $p_j$, that is, $\min(x_i, x_j) \le x_k \le \max(x_i, x_j)$ and $\min(y_i, y_j) \le y_k \le \max(y_i, y_j)$.
nodes.title: The ON-SEGMENT test

nodes.summary: If $d$ and $e$ are elements of a linearly ordered field that straddle zero, that is, they are nonzero with opposite signs, then $0 \le d / (d - e) \le 1$.
nodes.title: Zero-crossing parameter of values of opposite sign

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field and let $p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4 \in K^2$. The procedure SEGMENTS-INTERSECT$(p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4)$ returns true if and only if the closed segments $[p_1, p_2]$ and $[p_3, p_4]$ have a common point.
nodes.title: Correctness of SEGMENTS-INTERSECT

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field with a linear order, let $p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4 \in K^2$, and write $d_1 = \mathrm{DIRECTION}(p_3, p_4, p_1)$, $d_2 = \mathrm{DIRECTION}(p_3, p_4, p_2)$, $d_3 = \mathrm{DIRECTION}(p_1, p_2, p_3)$ and $d_4 = \mathrm{DIRECTION}(p_1, p_2, p_4)$. The value returned by SEGMENTS-INTERSECT$(p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4)$ is true if and only if at least one of the following holds: $d_1$ and $d_2$ are nonzero with…
nodes.title: SEGMENTS-INTERSECT as a Boolean formula

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field with a linear order and let $p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4 \in K^2$. In the cost model that charges one unit per DIRECTION computation and one per ON-SEGMENT test, SEGMENTS-INTERSECT$(p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4)$ costs at least $4$ and at most $8$.
nodes.title: Running time of SEGMENTS-INTERSECT

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field with a linear order and let $p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4 \in K^2$. CLRS's procedure SEGMENTS-INTERSECT$(p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4)$, which tests whether the segments $p_1p_2$ and $p_3p_4$ meet, first computes, at a cost of $4$, the directions $d_1 = \mathrm{DIRECTION}(p_3, p_4, p_1)$, $d_2 = \mathrm{DIRECTION}(p_3, p_4, p_2)$, $d_3 = \mathrm{DIRECTION}(p_1, p_2, p_3)$ and…
nodes.title: The SEGMENTS-INTERSECT procedure

nodes.summary: Let $d$ and $e$ be nonzero elements of a linearly ordered field. If $a d + b e = 0$ for some $a, b \ge 0$ in the field with $a + b = 1$, then $d$ and $e$ have opposite signs.
nodes.title: A vanishing convex combination of nonzero values forces opposite signs

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a linearly ordered field and $p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4 \in K^2$, and suppose the closed segments $[p_1, p_2]$ and $[p_3, p_4]$ have a common point. Then either $\mathrm{DIRECTION}(p_3, p_4, p_1)$ and $\mathrm{DIRECTION}(p_3, p_4, p_2)$ are nonzero with opposite signs and $\mathrm{DIRECTION}(p_1, p_2, p_3)$ and $\mathrm{DIRECTION}(p_1, p_2, p_4)$ are nonzero with opposite signs, or $p_1 \in [p_3, p_4]$, or…
nodes.title: Meeting segments cross properly or an endpoint lies on the other

nodes.summary: Two elements $d$ and $e$ of a field with a linear order straddle zero when $d > 0$ and $e < 0$, or $d < 0$ and $e > 0$; that is, $d$ and $e$ are nonzero with opposite signs.
nodes.title: Values of opposite sign

nodes.summary: If $d$ and $e$ are elements of a linearly ordered field that straddle zero, that is, they are nonzero with opposite signs, then $d - e \ne 0$.
nodes.title: Values of opposite sign have nonzero difference

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
